name: Energy Fuels news release: Commercial-Scale 'Heavy' Rare Earth Plant Now Under Construction in Utah
locator: White Mesa Mill current commercial capacity up to 1,000 tpa separated NdPr oxide; planned expansion designed to add up to approximately 20 tpa Tb, 120 tpa Dy, 140 tpa Sm, 20 tpa Eu, 140 tpa Gd oxides (fn.2: maximum design quantities, dependent on feed distribution and recoveries). name: Carester news release: Caremag, a subsidiary of Carester, has secured 216 million euros in financing to build its rare earth recycling and refining facility in France
locator: Financing EUR 216 million total: EUR 110 million from Japanese investors (JOGMEC and Iwatani Corporation), EUR 106 million from the French State. Feed: 2,000 tonnes of end-of-life magnets and 5,000 tonnes of mining concentrates annually. Output at full ramp-up: 800 tonnes of Neodymium and Praseodymium oxides and 600 tonnes of Dysprosium and Terbium oxides. Site at Lacq, south-west France; operations expected by late 2026. Long-term supply of heavy rare earth oxides to Japan via the Japan France Rare Earth Company joint venture. NOTE: this release gives Dy and Tb as a single combined 600 t figure; this release does not split them. name: Solvay press release: Solvay advances European rare earths production through capacity expansion (La Rochelle inauguration)
publisher: Solvay SA (Euronext Brussels and Paris: SOLB)
locator: p.1: inauguration of Solvay's rare earths production line for permanent magnets at La Rochelle; 'the biggest plant outside China capable of separating all rare earth materials'; commercial production of rare earths for permanent magnets begins 8 April 2025; 'first step toward meeting the objective of satisfying 30% of European demand by 2030'; feedstock sourced from a diverse range of suppliers, mining partners and recycled materials as mandated by the Critical Raw Materials Act; process reinvention to cut CO2 40% and halve water use by 2030. p.2 'About Solvay La Rochelle': founded 1948, 40-hectare site, over 300 employees. name: Neo Performance Materials news release: Neo Successfully Commissions Heavy Rare Earth Separation Production Line in Europe
locator: Commissioning of the HREE solvent extraction small-scale production line at the Silmet facility, Estonia; 'operating at nameplate capacity, with efforts now focused on delivering stable product purity prior to transitioning to routine production capacity'; first separated terbium and dysprosium process solutions ('pre-cursor products for metal making') from mixed rare earth carbonate feedstock, 'with all processing completed entirely in Europe'; complements Neo's European Permanent Magnet facility in Estonia, 'advancing through customer qualification milestones, with commercial production expected to ramp later in 2026'. NOTE: no tonnage capacity figure is disclosed; the line is explicitly small-scale.

name: Ucore Rare Metals news release: Ucore Launches US Department of Defense Funded $18.4 Million Commercial Rare Earth Refining Project
locator: US$18.4 million DoD Phase 2 Award formally kicked off, funding construction of Ucore's first commercial-scale RapidSX machine at the proposed Strategic Metals Complex (SMC), Alexandria, Louisiana, focused on HREEs; work culminates in commissioning, demonstration and 'Early Production' readiness of salable individual REE products. Phase 1 Award US$4 million: successful separation of terbium from dysprosium; payment of US$1,057,412 received, bringing Phase 1 payments to US$3,352,884 with US$647,116 remaining. Detailed design and engineering of commercial-scale RapidSX columns at the Kingston, Ontario Commercialization and Demonstration Facility; facility engineering field work and borehole drilling at Alexandria.

name: MP Materials news release: MP Materials Announces Transformational Public-Private Partnership with the Department of Defense to Accelerate U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Independence
locator: US$400 million DoD investment in a new series of convertible preferred stock, positioning DoD as largest shareholder at approximately 15% of common shares; US$1.0 billion of JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs financing for construction of the 10X Facility (commissioning expected 2028, taking total US magnet capacity to an estimated 10,000 metric tons); US$150 million DoD loan in connection with the plan to expand heavy rare earth separation capabilities at Mountain Pass, California; 10-year price floor commitment of US$110/kg for NdPr stockpiled or sold; DoD commitment to purchase 100% of 10X Facility magnet output for 10 years after construction.

name: Lynas Rare Earths ASX announcement: Lynas announces expanded Heavy Rare Earths separation facility in Malaysia

name: Aclara Resources news release: Aclara Announces Filing and Results of Feasibility Study for Its Flagship Carina Project
locator: p.1: FS titled 'NI 43-101 Technical Report & Feasibility Study on the Carina Project, Goias, Brazil', effective date 20 March 2026, by Hatch with named contributors, filed on SEDAR+; after-tax NPV8 approximately US$1.7 billion on Mineral Reserves. COO quote: 'the only company in the world to report heavy rare earth Mineral Reserves from ionic clays in accordance with NI 43-101'; metallurgy demonstrated via a continuously operated pilot plant; 'our path to market via our 100% owned separation facility that is planned to be built in Louisiana, USA'. Highlights: 18-year LOM; average annual production of 4,378 t REO contained in a mixed rare earth concentrate (MREC) with DyTb content 4.2% and NdPr content 27.2%; contained magnetic and strategic elements 156 t Dy, 27 t Tb, 1,191 t NdPr, 173 t Sm, 176 t Gd, 10 t Lu, 1,160 t Y; DyTb production 'equivalent to approximately 11.8% of China's 2024 estimated DyTb production'. Economics: after-tax IRR 26.9%, payback 2.9 years, construction capex US$678.2M plus US$102.7M contingency = US$780.9M (US$100.4M above PFS on FX, inflation and engineering accuracy); average annual commercial discount of US$314.4M, 34% of annual gross revenue, applied as a separation fee payable to Aclara's Louisiana separation project, whose NPV is EXCLUDED from the FS.

name: Ucore Rare Metals news release: Ucore Engineering Report Drives Optimized Commercial Deployment Plan for Louisiana Strategic Metals Complex
locator: Optimized Louisiana SMC configuration: an initial Machine A at approximately 600 tpa TREO plus three RapidSX Production Lines ('Trains') each capable of processing up to approximately 3,000 tpa TREO, for an overall SMC throughput capacity of approximately 9,600 tpa TREO; Machine A plus Production Line 1 gives approximately 3,600 tpa TREO. Enhanced Machine A capital cost US$60 million, of which US$18.4 million is Department of War (formerly DoD) funding. Installation, testing and commissioning of Machine A remains H1-2027. Framed as a move from a lowest initial build-cost concept toward a more robust commercial operating configuration. NOTE: all figures are TREO THROUGHPUT, not Dy/Tb product output; no per-element split is disclosed.

name: Brazilian Rare Earths / Carester joint news release: BRE and Carester sign 10-year Heavy Rare Earth Offtake and Partnership to deliver BRE's Rare Earth Separation Plant
publisher: Brazilian Rare Earths Limited (ASX:BRE) and Carester SAS
locator: Binding 10-year heavy rare earth offtake plus engineering and technical services agreement. name: Mkango Resources news release: Results of Updated Feasibility Study for the Songwe Hill Rare Earths Project in Malawi and Pre-Feasibility Results for the Proposed Pulawy Rare Earth Separation Plant in Poland
locator: 21pp. Pulawy PFS by PRODEO Consulting (Pty) Ltd, base date 25 Feb 2026, AACE Class 4 (+/-25%). Base case: 'expanded 30 000 t/a MREC (45% TREO, wet basis) feed with 100% NdPr separation option'; 'Initial feed for the plant at 13,430 t/a REO throughput capacity'. Capex US$212,354,912 including US$35.4M contingency. Opex 'US$2.142 per kilogram of TREO in MREC to produce the designated product suite', US$28,699,135/yr. NPV US$779.1M at 10% nominal, IRR 39.7% nominal / 36.3% real, payback 2.12 years. Milestones: engineering start April 2026, procurement September 2026, construction April 2027, commissioning October 2028, ramp-up Q2 2029 ending Q1 2030; 'Life of operations from the first year of full production is 29 years (2030 - 2058)'. CRITICAL - PRODUCT SUITE: the only definition is the payability assumption, 'Payability factors of Nd oxide, Pr oxide and NdPr oxide 100%; SEGH carbonate 75%; LaCe carbonate 100% at US$2/kg'. Dy and Tb are NOT separate products; they report to a mixed SEGH (Sm-Eu-Gd-Heavies) carbonate. The study frames options as NdPr split only (0%, 50%, 100%), with no HREE circuit variants. NO Dy/Tb tonnage is disclosed for Pulawy. Songwe Hill (Malawi, a separate asset): 'production averaging 5,954 tonnes per year total rare earth oxides (TREO) for the first full five years of production, including 1,953 tonnes per year of neodymium and praseodymium oxides, and 56 tonnes per year of dysprosium and terbium oxides, in a MREC grading 55% TREO (dry basis).'

name: Mkango Resources RNS: Mkango's Pulawy Rare Earth Separation Project Announced as a Strategic Project under EU Critical Raw Materials Act
locator: p.2, section 'Pulawy Rare Earth Separation Project': 'The proposed plant will target production of 2,000 tonnes/year of neodymium and/or praseodymium oxides, and 50 tonnes/year of dysprosium and terbium oxides. Lanthanum cerium carbonate will also be produced at the site.' Designated one of 47 EU strategic projects under Regulation (EU) 2024/1252. CAUTION: this is the ORIGINAL non-expanded design and predates the 19 Mar 2026 PFS by a year; the PFS neither restates the 50 t/yr figure nor lists separated Dy/Tb oxide among the product suite.

name: Aclara Resources news release: Aclara Announces Results from Technical Reports on its Integrated Heavy Rare Earths Supply Chain (Project Dynamo scoping study)
locator: Companion release issued the SAME DAY as the Carina FS release. p.1 defines study status: only Carina is NI 43-101; Project Dynamo is a SCOPING STUDY and the metals/alloys project is FEL-2 (pre-feasibility level). Lead engineers Hatch / L3 Process Development. Project Dynamo section, 'Annual Average Production': 'Dy oxide (>99.5%): 148 tonnes. Tb oxide (>99.5%): 25 tonnes. NdPr oxide (>99.5%): 1,131 tonnes.' Table 1 note 1: annual average excludes the first ramp-up year and last ramp-down year. Feed basis: 'Feedstock is assumed to be sourced exclusively from the Carina Project'. Byproducts as mixed carbonates (not separated oxides): ~173 t Sm, 8 t Eu, 177 t Gd, 1,160 t Y, 31 t Ho, 88 t Er, 12 t Tm, 73 t Yb, 10 t Lu. 'Strong Economics': after-tax NPV US$470M at 8.0%, IRR 25.2%, payback 3.3 years; 'Construction Capex of US$277 million, plus US$52 million in working capital'; 'Average annual net revenue of US$175 million and EBITDA of approximately US$117 million, supported by a processing fee of US$40 per kilogram of TREO processed, compared to low average Opex of US$12.6 per kilogram of TREO processed'; US$46.4M Louisiana incentives. Site: 82-acre LED Certified Site, Lake Charles corridor / Port of Vinton, ~80-year lease option, Entergy 34.5 kV, demand <5 MW of ~6 MW confirmed. Permitting: air quality, industrial wastewater, stormwater; 'Key approvals are targeted by October 2026 to enable groundbreaking currently slated for the end of 2026.' Path to production: Q3 2026 FEL-3 basic engineering, Q4 2026 long-lead award and site works, Q1 2027-Q1 2028 construction, Q2 2028 pre-commissioning and ramp-up. Phasing: Phase 1 NdPr/Dy/Tb; Phase 2 Y, Gd, Sm; Phase 3 Ho, Er, Tm, Yb, Lu.

name: Aclara Resources news release: Aclara to Build First Heavy Rare Earths Separation Facility in U.S. with a Secured Sustainable Ionic Clay Feed by Mid-2028
locator: 'Key Project Highlights' bullet 5: 'Annual production upon the successful development of the Company's ionic clay deposits in Brazil and Chile is anticipated to be 200 tpy (Dy), 30 tpy (Tb) and 1,400 tpy (NdPr) of separated high-purity oxides, representing approximately 14% of China's official DyTb production.' CRITICAL: this is a CARINA + PENCO (Brazil + Chile) feed basis - a different and larger basis than the 148 t Dy / 25 t Tb Carina-only figure in the Apr 2026 Dynamo scoping study. The two are separate scenarios, not revisions of each other. 'Project Development': US$277M, 82-acre LED site at Port of Vinton; incentives ITEP US$29.3M, HIP US$11.6M, infrastructure grant US$3.0M, FastStart US$2.5M = US$46.4M.

name: Aclara Resources news release: Aclara Secures Tax Exemption Approval of Over US$20 Million for its U.S. Heavy Rare Earth Separation Facility in Louisiana
locator: 'the State of Louisiana has granted final approval under the Industrial Tax Exemption Program (ITEP) for the Company's planned heavy rare earth separation facility at the Port of Vinton, Louisiana.' ITEP contract executed by Governor Landry; 80% ad valorem exemption for 5 years plus a 5-year renewal option; approximately US$4.2M/yr and approximately US$20.8M over the initial term - LOWER than the US$29.3M estimated in the Oct 2025 release, so use this figure. Groundbreaking target Q4 2026. Pilot plant expected to provide approximately two years of operating data before production.

name: Ucore Rare Metals news release: Ucore Verifies Louisiana RapidSX Equipment Scale-Up Configurations
locator: Most explicit statement of the capacity basis: 'Pending construction completion, commissioning, qualification, and receipt of all required funding and permits, Ucore's Louisiana SMC shall be capable of accepting mixed rare earth carbonate ("MREC") and mixed rare earth oxide ("MREO") from Western-friendly feedstock sources and processing up to approximately 9,600 tpa of contained TREOs.' Confirms every published SMC number is CONTAINED TREO IN FEEDSTOCK, not product output. The 28 May 2026 engineering report lists the product suite - 'NdPr, Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, SmEuGd ("SEG"), Tb, Dy, rare earth oxide products, and intermediates' - with NO tonnage attached to any element.

name: Ucore Rare Metals news release: Ucore Rare Metals and Meteoric Resources Sign MOU for Offtake of Caldeira Project MREC in Brazil to USA Oxide Production Project
locator: 'Key Provisions of the MOU', bullet 2: 'Once the Parties are in production they envision that Ucore will purchase a minimum quantity of 3,000MT of TREO annually from Caldeira. This could represent over 900MT of NdPr, approximately 6MT of Tb and 24MT of Dy.' CONTAINED-IN-CONCENTRATE under a NON-BINDING MOU, not SMC output capacity. Carried forward verbatim in Ucore's MD&A for the three months ended 31 Mar 2026 (prepared 29 May 2026), p.13. Covers roughly 31% of the SMC's 9,600 tpa nameplate throughput; never restated against the current configuration. Implies a Caldeira basket of ~0.8% Dy and ~0.2% Tb of TREO - that is Caldeira's assemblage, NOT a design-basis feed assemblage for the SMC.

name: Lynas Rare Earths Limited 2026 Annual Report (lodged with Appendix 4E)
locator: Directors' Report, Review of Operations, section 'Lynas USA', p.16: 'Lynas signed a binding Letter of Intent with the U.S. Government in March 2026 for the supply of approximately US$96 million of light and heavy rare earth oxides over a 4 year period... Funding for the supply agreement has been reallocated from funds previously intended for the construction of a HRE facility in Texas WHICH WILL NO LONGER PROCEED. The floor price for supply of NdPr oxide will be US$110/kg.' Note B.3 'Impairment of non-current assets', p.107: 'There was $1.7m of impairment expense recognised on specific assets at during FY26 (FY25: $1.0m)' - sits in the buildings/plant column of the Note B.1 PP&E table with NO US attribution. Note B.1 PP&E, p.102: 'Government grants received ... (6,925)' i.e. A$6.925m netted against assets under construction. Note A.1, p.92: single reportable segment under AASB 8, so there is no geographic non-current-asset breakdown and no US asset line. Note A.4.4, p.98: unrecognised deferred tax assets, gross revenue losses, United States A$3,911k (2025: A$3,545k). Note E.1: contingent liabilities list only the Malaysian licence bond - no clawback or repayment contingency disclosed; capital commitments at 30 June 2026 nil. 'Seadrift' appears ZERO times in this document; 'Texas' appears exactly once, in the sentence quoted above. There is no discontinued-operations, held-for-sale or derecognition note, and no standalone cancellation announcement was ever made.

name: Lynas Rare Earths ASX announcement: Lynas and US DoW Sign Letter of Intent for Rare Earth Supply
locator: p.1: 'This offtake agreement follows the mutual decision to modify the original agreement between Lynas and the DoW based on significant uncertainty as to whether the construction of the Heavy Rare Earth processing facility at Seadrift, Texas would proceed.' Counterparty is the US Department of War, contracting via subsidiary Lynas USA LLC. This is the pivot event; the definitive 'will no longer proceed' language appears five months later in the FY2026 Annual Report.

name: Lynas Rare Earths Limited 2025 Annual Report
locator: Section 'Lynas USA', p.15: 'A contribution by the U.S. Department of Defence of approximately US$258m is currently allocated to the Seadrift facility.' and 'The contract is an expenditure-based contract under which all of Lynas' properly allocable construction costs in respect of the facility will be reimbursed.' Also: 'Lynas is yet to commence construction or operations in the USA and had no USA employees in FY25.' CORRECTS the widely-repeated trade-press figure of approximately US$288m 'received' - the disclosed figure is US$258m ALLOCATED under an expenditure-reimbursement contract, not received.

locator: Item 1 Business, 'Colorado Facility': 'We expect that this facility, with 500+ planned mixer/settlers should become one of the largest and most sophisticated solvent extraction ("SX") demo facilities in the nation.' and 'The Colorado Facility is not a commercial production facility, but rather develops and refines the technologies that, with success, would be applied at the Round Top Project.' name: Lynas Corporation ASX announcement: Increase in Mt Weld Resource Estimates
locator: p.3 Table 5, 'REO DISTRIBUTION OF MINERAL RESOURCES', by deposit as a percentage of TREO. Central Lanthanide Deposit (CLD): Terbium Oxide 0.09%, Dysprosium Oxide 0.25%, Yttrium Oxide 0.76%. THIS IS THE LAST PER-ELEMENT MINERAL RESOURCE ASSEMBLAGE LYNAS EVER PUBLISHED - every resource statement from 2015 onward gives tonnes, TREO% and contained TREO only. Consistent earlier vintages: the 2003 Annual Report (ASX 20 Oct 2003, https://wcsecure.weblink.com.au/pdf/LYC/00391467.pdf, p.6 Table 1) gives Tb4O7 0.09% and Dy2O3 0.16% of TREO at grades of 0.015 wt% and 0.027 wt%; the 3 Mar 2008 resource announcement (.../00819169.pdf p.4 Table 3) gives Central Zone Tb 0.09% / Dy 0.16% and Southern Zone Tb 0.32% / Dy 1.56%; the 5 Sep 2010 announcement (.../01095422.pdf p.5 Table 5, a raster image that does not extract with pdftotext) gives CLD Tb 0.13% / Dy 0.31% and Duncan Tb 0.29% / Dy 1.36%. The 13 Jun 2012 Duncan update (.../01305353.pdf p.2 Table 3) additionally gives indicative annual production of Terbium Oxide 62 tpa and Dysprosium Oxide 300 tpa. THE KEY STRUCTURAL FACT: the CLD, which is the main ore source, is LREE-dominant at ~0.25-0.31% Dy2O3 of TREO, while the separate Duncan deposit is four to five times heavier at ~1.27-1.36%.

name: USA Rare Earth Form 8-K: Share Purchase and Investment Agreement with Carester SAS (and Exhibit 99.1 press release)
locator: Accession 0001213900-26-080645, Items 3.02/7.01/8.01/9.01. Item 8.01: 'On July 22, 2026, USA Rare Earth, Inc. ... entered into a Share Purchase and Investment Agreement ... by and among (i) Frederic Carencotte (the Founder), (ii) CareInvest, (iii) USAR, (iv) InfraVia CMF Invest S.a r.l., and (v) Carester SAS'. Total New Investor subscription EUR 45,000,225 in Preferred Shares RR; USAR subscribes 48,149 shares for EUR 10,833,525 cash plus a Contribution in Kind of 51,852 shares for EUR 11,666,700 paid in USAR common stock; Secondary Transaction 22,222 shares for EUR 4,999,950; RHODIA EXIT - USAR takes 55,555 shares for EUR 12,499,875 'resulting in the full exit of Solvay as a shareholder of Carester'. 'Upon completion ... USAR will hold 177,778 Preferred Shares RR, representing approximately 13.6% of Carester's share capital' (up from the 12.5% contemplated in the 9 Apr 2026 term sheet). Completion expected Q3 2026, conditional on the Rhodia share purchase agreement; NOT CLOSED as at the latest EDGAR filing of 31 Aug 2026. Q2 2026 10-Q totals it as EUR 40.0m (~US$45.7m). FEEDSTOCK CLAIM - Exhibit 99.1 press release subheadline: 'Gives Carester Access to USA Rare Earth Feedstock from Serra Verde and Round Top', and body: 'In turn, Carester will have access to USA Rare Earth feedstock sources, including Serra Verde and the Round Top deposit in Texas.' The April 2026 investor deck adds '15-year supply: excess concentrate from Round Top or other USAR sources to Caremag / 15-year offtake: USAR takes oxides produced from its contributed concentrate'. FOUR CRITICAL QUALIFICATIONS: (1) the feedstock language appears ONLY in furnished press releases and decks, never in the filed Item 8.01 description of what was actually signed - no supply, offtake or technology agreement is filed as an exhibit; (2) Serra Verde was not USAR's asset when the claim was made and the merger had not closed as at 1 Sep 2026; (3) Serra Verde Phase 1 output is 100% committed to a US-government-backed SPV under a separate 15-year offtake, and no primary document reconciles how Carester obtains it; (4) Round Top is pre-production, expected 'late 2028'. NO TONNAGE is given for the USAR-to-Caremag supply in any primary document.

name: USA Rare Earth Form 8-K and Serra Verde press release: satisfaction of the US SIIE offtake conditions precedent
locator: Offtake dated 20 Apr 2026 between SV Management Switzerland AG and US SIIE, LLC, 'a special purpose vehicle capitalized by the U.S. government and private capital sources' (DEFM14A risk factors). CONDITIONS PRECEDENT SATISFIED 21-24 Aug 2026 - Serra Verde: the SPV 'has put in place its capitalization arrangements and it is now required to start accepting deliveries which the Company expects to make early in fourth quarter of 2026'; the agreement is 'now in force and in full effect'. SCOPE: '100% of Phase I production from the Pela Ema facility of Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb ... on a take-or-pay basis', subject to unspecified 'limited carve-outs'. CARVE-OUTS THAT MATTER: 'The Company also has the ability to monetize elements that do not currently form part of the Products, including Yttrium' - and yttrium is 42% of LOM basket VALUE. A potential Phase 2 (approximately +6,400 tpa TREO) is NOT covered. FLOOR PRICES: 'Terbium US$2,050 per kg; Dysprosium US$575 per kg; Neodymium US$110 per kg; Praseodymium US$110 per kg', escalated 2% annually, with 70% of any excess of the market index over the floor payable to the seller. TERM - CONFLICTING CHARACTERISATIONS: the legal formulation is 'the earlier of (i) the date on which deliveries ... equal the rare earth products produced from 198,000,000 metric tons of run-of-mine ore and (ii) the date that is 20 years after ... the Commercial Operations Date', which has NOT yet occurred; the universal '15-year' framing in USAR and Serra Verde marketing is not reconciled to it in any primary document and should be treated as shorthand. ENFORCEMENT: US SIIE holds a call option over ALL equity interests in SVRE, triggered by events including breach of the offtake's change-of-control provisions. RESIDUAL RISK: the US$500m senior debt facility funding the SPV's purchases 'has not been documented, closed or funded' and its commitment expires 31 Dec 2026. The offtake agreement itself has never been filed as an exhibit - all detail is narrative summary.

name: Mkango Rare Earths Ltd Form F-4/A registration statement (Crown PropTech merger)
locator: THE PULAWY FEED ENVELOPE, and it is in the SEC record rather than on mkango.ca or SEDAR+. Business-Overview: 'Mixed rare earth carbonate (MREC) produced at our Songwe Hill rare earths project will serve as the initial Feedstock ... To the extent the Proposed Pulawy Separation Plant has additional capacity, we plan to source MREC from other rare earth projects and market suppliers for processing and separation into rare earth oxides.' Business-Competition: 'Because the Proposed Pulawy Separation Plant is expected to rely on third-party carbonate feed in addition to the MREC sourced from Songwe Hill, we face competition from other processing companies seeking to secure comparable feedstock streams.' QUANTIFIED in the 19 Mar 2026 PFS release p.16: Songwe supplies 45% of throughput in the first five years 'with the remaining 55% sourced from market', priced at a 15% discount to contained REO value for Songwe carbonate versus 25% for market-sourced. NO FEED SPECIFICATION IS PUBLISHED anywhere - zero occurrences of impurity, radionuclide, Th/U, moisture or elemental limits across the F-4/A, the 489-page S-K 1300 technical report summary, the PFS release or the June 2026 deck; the Pulawy PFS itself was never filed and is not required to be, since Pulawy is not a mineral project. Mkango concedes the gap in a risk factor: 'third-party Feedstock may differ materially in chemical composition, impurity levels, and physical characteristics from Songwe Hill MREC. Variability in Feedstock quality could create metallurgical challenges, require process adjustments, increase reagent consumption, and reduce recovery rates.' NO third-party feed agreement exists: 'There can be no assurance that we will be able to identify, negotiate, and secure long-term supply agreements with third-party Feedstock providers on commercially acceptable terms, or at all.'

name: Aclara Resources Annual Information Form FY2025 and 2026 MD&As (Project Dynamo feed basis)
locator: PROJECT DYNAMO IS CAPTIVE BY DESIGN. AIF Item 3.1: 'Aclara Technologies intends to source high-purity mixed MREC from the Company's mining projects', repeated at Item 4.1; Q2 2026 MD&A: 'Aclara Technologies aims to source SPREC from Aclara's mining projects'; identical boilerplate closes every 2025-26 release - 'This facility will process mixed rare earth carbonates sourced from Aclara's mineral resource projects'. The Oct 2025 site release is broader but still bounded and future-conditional: capacity expansion 'to process material from other ionic clay deposits or compatible feedstocks in the future'. NO FEED SPEC of any kind is published. FALSE POSITIVE TO DISCOUNT: the DOE award 'AI-Enabled Process Optimization for Multi-Feed Rare Earth Separation' - Aclara defines multi-feed as 'Simulation of multiple feedstocks beyond the Carina Project, such as the Penco Module MREC', i.e. both feeds are Aclara-owned.

name: Neo Performance Materials Investor Presentation, September 2026, and 2026 AIF (Silmet feed basis)
locator: SILMET IS THE ONLY GENUINE MERCHANT SEPARATOR OF THE THREE EUROPEAN PLANTS. Slide 19 'European Rare Earth Separation Capabilities': 'One of the only non-captive operators of a large-scale light rare earth separation facility, strengthening Western supply chains'. NO class-level 'capable of processing X' sentence exists; the 2026 AIF offers only a source-GEOGRAPHY envelope - inputs 'can be purchased from a number of suppliers in Australia (via Malaysia), United States, Myanmar, Russia and China'. The de facto envelope is documented instead by an accumulation of NAMED feeds: monazite-derived RE carbonate from Energy Fuels' White Mesa (definitive supply agreement and commercial shipments, 2021, 'successfully processed trial quantities'); rare earth ore or mineral concentrate from Sarfartoq, Greenland (binding offtake, 2023); concentrate from Hastings Yangibana (non-binding HoA, 2023); ionic-clay MREC from Meteoric Caldeira (non-binding MOU, 2024, 3,000 t TREO/yr); and MREC tolling for Carester (binding term sheet, 31 Aug 2026, no volume, term, pricing or specification disclosed). TWO CORRECTIONS TO CIRCULATING CLAIMS: (1) LOPARITE IS REFUTED - the word appears zero times in the 2025 AIF, 2026 AIF, Q2 2026 MD&A and Sept 2026 deck; Neo describes the Russian supply only as 'rare earth feedstock from a Russian supplier'. (2) 'Ionic clay' appears zero times in those same documents. LIVE CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: the 2026 AIF Environmental Matters section states 'Silmet no longer processes feedstock that contains naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM) but does produce tantalum and niobium using alternative feedstocks that it is permitted to process' - worded as a facility-level assertion, it cuts directly against monazite-derived MREC, which carries Th/U, and against the Energy Fuels history.

name: Lynas Malaysia operating licence conditions: MOSTI media release (2 Mar 2026), and the 2023 licence renewal and variation announcements
publisher: Kementerian Sains, Teknologi dan Inovasi (MOSTI) Malaysia; Lynas Rare Earths Ltd (ASX:LYC)
locator: THE REGULATORY FEED CONSTRAINT, AND IT HAS CHANGED SHAPE. PRECEDENT that the AELB can bar an entire feed class - ASX 14 Feb 2023: 'The operating licence has been renewed with no change to the licence conditions ... These conditions prohibit the import and processing of lanthanide concentrate after 1 July 2023.' PERMISSION WAS THEN ORIGIN-SPECIFIC - ASX 24 Oct 2023: 'Lynas Malaysia has been issued with a variation to its operating licence which allows the continued importation and processing of Lanthanide Concentrate from Lynas' Mt Weld mine in Western Australia ... valid until 2 March 2026.' THE CURRENT LICENCE (3 Mar 2026 to 2 Mar 2036) CONTAINS NO FEEDSTOCK-ORIGIN OR IMPORT RESTRICTION - the Mt-Weld-only wording is gone from the FY2026 Annual Report section 2.4. That is a LOOSENING. The binding constraint has moved from feed ORIGIN to RESIDUE: per MOSTI, no new permanent disposal facility may be built for Water Leach Purification residue above control limits, and after the first five years the production of radioactive residue must cease entirely, with residue neutralised via thorium extraction to below 1 Bq/g. Lynas's rendering, FY2026 Annual Report Directors' Report p.16 and section 2.4 p.24: 'Lynas Malaysia is required to implement an alternative cracking process so that the facility no longer produces WLP residue with an activity concentration above 1 Bq/g after 2 March 2031, with the modification to commence based on an agreed plan by March 2028.' INFERENCE, NOT DISCLOSURE: WLP arises from sulphuric-acid cracking and leaching of thorium-bearing rare earth MINERAL CONCENTRATE, so a hard post-2031 ban on >1 Bq/g WLP is functionally a constraint on monazite-class concentrate feed at Kuantan unless the alternative cracking process succeeds - while MREC and ionic-clay carbonate feeds enter downstream of cracking and leaching and carry little NORM. That is consistent with Lynas pointing at Malaysian ionic clay. A further gate is open: on 23 Jun 2026 the Department of Environment requested an updated EIA for the proposed Malaysian expansion.

name: Lynas Rare Earths ASX announcement: Lynas Inks Agreement for Malaysian Ionic Clay Feedstock (Menteri Besar Inc, Kelantan)
locator: THE ONLY NAMED THIRD-PARTY FEED COUNTERPARTY LYNAS MALAYSIA HAS EVER DISCLOSED. Non-binding MoU 'for the supply of mixed rare earths carbonate (MREC) from Menteri Besar (MB) Inc., the strategic investment arm of the Kelantan State Government', providing 'a framework for MB Inc. and Lynas to negotiate a definitive agreement for the supply MREC feedstock to the Lynas Malaysia advanced materials plant in Kuantan once the project commences production'. CEO Lacaze: 'Malaysia's ionic clay deposits have excellent potential as future feedstocks for Lynas Malaysia, particularly given their high proportion of Heavy Rare Earths' and 'We look forward to working with MB Inc. to ensure that the MREC it produces meets the high environmental and technical standards required by Lynas' - i.e. Lynas reserved a quality gate. Structure is PURCHASE of MREC, not tolling. STALENESS FLAG: 'Kelantan', 'Menteri Besar' and 'MB Inc' appear NOWHERE in the FY2026 Annual Report or any FY26 quarterly or results presentation; FY26 language has reverted to generic 'identification of potential new feedstock sources'. The MoU never reached definitive agreement and has dropped out of disclosure.

name: MP Materials Q3 2025 earnings call - COO remarks on third-party feedstock classes (TRANSCRIPT, NOT A FILING)
publisher: MP Materials Corp. (NYSE:MP) - machine-generated transcript, publisher not MP
locator: THE ONLY MATERIAL-CLASS FEED ENVELOPE MP HAS EVER GIVEN, and it exists only on an earnings call. Michael Rosenthal, Founder and COO, answering an analyst who asked whether there are concentrates the heavy circuit cannot process: 'Certainly, to the extent we got an SEG+, that would be easier than processing a full mixed rare earth carbonate with lights and heavies. Our circuit can handle, because we have all of the capabilities, either one of those. We will look at the economics and the distribution and compare those to other alternatives.' Prepared remarks add: 'we are actively engaged with a number of different and different types of potential feedstock providers to supplement our own contained HRE content.' PROVENANCE CAVEAT - THIS IS WHY THE SOURCE IS TYPED 'OTHER' AND CITED AT LOW CONFIDENCE: the quote comes from a machine-generated third-party transcript, not from MP. MP does not publish transcripts. Verify against MP's own Q3 2025 webcast replay before treating the wording as verbatim. NOTHING MORE SPECIFIC HAS BEEN SAID SINCE: the Q2 2026 call reverted to 'a site that is capable of handling feedstocks of different type and purity', naming no class. POSITIVE NULLS across MP's whole EDGAR corpus: 'monazite concentrate' 0 hits, 'ionic clay' 0 hits, MREO/MREC 0 hits in any 2025-26 filing, 'recycled feedstock' 0, 'feed agreement' 0; no named inbound feed counterparty, supply agreement, MOU, LOI or testwork announcement exists anywhere. WORDING REGRESSION WORTH WATCHING: the Q3 2025 10-Q described Upstream 60K as including 'the ability to process alternative feedstocks and upgrade lower-grade feedstocks'; the FY2025 10-K and both 2026 10-Qs DROPPED 'alternative feedstocks', replacing it with better usage of lower-grade Mountain Pass ore - a narrowing to own ore. The Q2 2026 gadolinium offtake was purely OUTBOUND and sourced from MP's own SEG stream; no inbound feed deal accompanied it.

name: Ucore Rare Metals MD&A for the three months ended 31 March 2026, and Defense Metals MD&A series FY2024-FY2025
publisher: Ucore Rare Metals Inc. (TSXV:UCU); Defense Metals Corp (TSXV:DEFN)
locator: THIS SOURCE EXISTS TO RECORD A CONTRADICTION WITH UCORE'S OWN WICHEEDA QUALIFICATION NEWS RELEASE. p.19, immediately above the seven-campaign table: 'Seven demonstration campaigns were completed as follows, all starting with nearly two tonnes of a heavy mixed rare earth oxide feed source containing both heavy and light REEs' - SX-1 through SX-7, 18 Dec 2023 to 24 Jan 2026, 5,717 hours, 1.76 t REO equivalent processed. Ucore's entire two-year DoD demonstration programme therefore ran on a SINGLE heavy MREO feed source, and Wicheeda material is not identified as having been processed in any campaign. Ucore's MD&A series says only that Defense Metals 'sent a mixed rare earth carbonate sample to the Company's RapidSX Demo Plant' - unchanged boilerplate carried for over two years, with NO date, mass, TREO grade, impurity or radionuclide content, and NO RESULT EVER REPORTED. The tense shifted from 'will send' (Q1 2024) to 'sent' (FY2024 MD&A, Apr 2025) and has not changed since. DEFENSE METALS' OWN FILINGS NEVER MENTION A SAMPLE TO UCORE AT ALL: every MD&A from Feb 2024 to Jul 2025 carries one boilerplate sentence about the MOU and nothing more. Its only sample-shipment disclosure is an OCTOBER 2023 multi-recipient distribution to UNNAMED 'select major processors, refiners, and metals traders located in Europe, Asia and North America' - which predates the January 2024 Ucore MOU and is never linked to it - and its FY2025 MD&A still reads 'Discussions with the sample recipients regarding their individual test results and their assessments of the samples are ongoing', 21 months on, with no results ever reported. UNRESOLVED: Ucore's Aug 2026 release describes a campaign on 'approximately five tonnes of mixed rare earth carbonate derived from North American bastnaesite source material'; Wicheeda is a bastnaesite carbonatite, but Ucore does not name the source and 5 t is an order of magnitude above a sample. Do not assert the link. NOTE: the Defense Metals NI 43-101 PFS technical report (effective 28 Feb 2025), the most likely home for Wicheeda MREC impurity and Th/U assays, is on SEDAR+ only and was unreachable (HTTP 403).

name: ABx Group ASX announcements: maiden Deep Leads mixed rare earth carbonate, assay, and distribution to Ucore
locator: THE BEST-CHARACTERISED THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL SENT TO UCORE IN THIS GRAPH. 2 Mar 2026, 'Evaluation of Maiden MREC Sample by Customers': 'Samples of the maiden MREC have been dispatched to multiple prospective customers. This includes Ucore Rare Metals Inc. ... ABx and Ucore have a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to develop a collaborative pathway for the supply of mixed rare earth carbonates from Australia to Ucore.' QUANTITY (17 Jun 2026): '10 gram samples of the maiden MREC distributed to six potential customers in Australia and North America for evaluation' - ten grams, to six recipients. FULL ASSAY (2 Dec 2025, Table 4, normalised): TREO 96.53%, NdPr 26.71%, DyTb 4.54%, Y2O3 26.11%; impurities Al2O3 0.43%, CaO 0.50%, Fe2O3 0.20%, SiO2 0.64%, U3O8 0.0053%, ThO2 below 0.002%, total impurities 3.47%. Source material a 100 kg bulk sample from trial pit DLP002, processed by ammonium sulfate leach, impurity removal and precipitation to yield 72 g of MREC. Radioactivity (ANSTO gamma spectrometry): every radionuclide below 0.5 Bq/g, within the IAEA bulk exemption limit of 1.0 Bq/g. MOU TERMS (4 Sep 2024): 'The intent is for Ucore to obtain first right of refusal for 50% of ABx annual volume for a minimum period of five years, subject to the agreement of commercial terms.' A presentation slide notes 'Ucore favours ABx's REE project because it is enriched in Tb & Dy'. RESULTS ARE QUALITATIVE ONLY: 'ABx received highly favourable feedback on its maiden MREC from Ucore' - no recoveries, purities or separated products, and ABx NEVER STATES WHICH UCORE FACILITY received the sample. Contrast a different customer, where ABx did report a finding: 'RETi advised that the Deep Leads MREC is of high purity and is suitable for the RETi process.'

locator: p.2: 'Bulk MREC samples have been provided to a range of groups for separation testwork and product qualification, including existing partners Neo Performance Materials in Europe, Ucore and MTM in the United States. Other potential offtake partners in these regions and Asia have also received samples of MREC for product qualification.' Meteoric describes 'Ucore ... in the United States' while Ucore's operating demo plant is in Kingston, Ontario - the receiving facility is NOT DISCLOSED.
